sentences.text: Estimates of Lanzhousaurus vary, with some sources suggesting a length of 10 meters and a weight of 6 tons, while others propose a slightly lighter mass of 4 tons.
The only known species, Lanzhousaurus magnidens, is represented by a partial skeleton discovered in the Lanzhou Bed within the Hekou Group of Gansu province, China.

This dinosaur is distinguished by its astonishingly huge teeth, which reached 14 centimeters in length on a lower jaw measuring one meter, a feature not seen in other iguanodontids that typically have many smaller teeth.
The mandible exceeded one meter in length, and the animal possessed compressed metacarpals II and IV along with moderately high neural spines that created a low profile at the hips.
These teeth are the largest discovered in any known herbivorous dinosaur.
The tooth enamel of Lanzhousaurus grew very rapidly.
The genus Lanzhousaurus was formally described by You, Ji, and Li in 2005.

The massive dentition indicates that Lanzhousaurus was a styracosternan iguanodont, representing a previously unknown lineage of massively built quadrupedal ornithopods alongside Lurdusaurus from Niger.
This discovery implies a close connection between Eurasia and Africa during the Early Cretaceous.
Phylogenetic analyses recovered Lanzhousaurus as a non-hadrosauriform styracosternan member of the Ankylopollexia, with Styracosterna serving as its parent group.
